answers.answer: For campaign progress use {charity.name}, {charity.link}, {charity.raised}, {charity.target}, {charity.percent} and {charity.bar}. For donations use {charity.donations.count} and {charity.donations.latest}. None of them takes an argument, so each is typed exactly as shown, for example {charity.name}: {charity.raised} of {charity.target} {charity.bar}. Thank you, {charity.donations.latest}!
answers.quote: None of these helpers takes an input, so type each one exactly as shown.

answers.answer: You need to know how to use braces in a reply, which the Variables and templates page covers. The bot also needs the Twitch permission channel:read:charity, which the first sign-in does not ask for. A campaign must be running on your Twitch channel. Both requirements are stated in the opening paragraphs and in the section The Twitch permission they need.
answers.quote: To read your campaign, the bot needs your Twitch permission channel:read:charity.

answers.answer: It worked when the reply shows values, as in the example output. It failed when a helper prints its braces as typed. The causes table separates the three failures: Needs attention shows the missing permission, Twitch shows no running campaign, or Twitch did not answer. The progress helpers describe the whole campaign. The donation helpers give the count (capped at 100) and the newest donor with the amount.
answers.quote: When a helper has nothing to show, it prints exactly as you typed it, braces and all.

answers.answer: Use {charity.raised}, {charity.target} and {charity.bar} (or {charity.percent}) for progress and {charity.donations.latest} for the latest donation. With no active campaign, every charity helper prints as typed with its braces, so the command should be used only on charity streams. When a campaign is running but has no donations yet, {charity.donations.latest} prints as typed, so the thank-you part is left out until the first donation.
answers.quote: With no campaign running, every helper in the reply prints as typed, so use the command only on your charity streams.

answers.answer: I would have to guess how to grant the missing permission. The page says the permission must be granted, but no step names where or how, and the only control it names on the Needs attention item is Dismiss. The cost is that a reader whose helpers print braces knows the cause but cannot fix it from this page. I also learn only after the permission section that a dismissed item hides the warning, so an empty list proves nothing. That costs a reread of the causes table.
answers.quote: Until the permission is granted, every charity helper prints as typed, and the rest of the reply still shows.

answers.answer: Read aloud, the block characters in the example outputs are noise. The prose sentence that describes the bar in words carries the meaning, so the cost is small.
answers.quote: In words, the example bar is four filled blocks, then six pale blocks, then 42%.

findings: The page says the charity helpers print as typed until the channel:read:charity permission is granted, but no step tells the reader where or how to grant it, and the only control it names on the Needs attention item is Dismiss.
